# The History of Cartography

Cartography is the study and practice of making maps. Combining science,
aesthetics and technique, cartography builds on the premise that reality can be
modeled in ways that communicate spatial information effectively.

The earliest known maps are of the stars, not the earth. Dots dating to
16,500 years ago found on the walls of the Lascaux caves map out part of the
night sky, including the three bright stars known today as the Summer Triangle.

Medieval maps of the world are called *mappa mundi*. Modern cartography is
integrated with geographic information science and constitutes many theoretical
and practical foundations of geographic information systems.
